Theme

Latin word

amō

amō, amāre, amāvī, amātum

verb, first conjugation

love

In this lexicon

  • love

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: nōn enim concēdō tibi plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō; Ter. Ph. 478: omnēs vōs amō

  • Tē amō: I love you

    classical

  • Multum tē amō.: thank you

    classical

Examples

  • nōn enim concēdō tibi plūs ut illum amēs quam ipse amō

    For I won’t grant that you love him more than I do.Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7

    In the entry for love

  • Mī Geta, omnēs vōs amō.

    My dear Geta, I love you all.Ter. Ph. 478

    In the entry for love

  • dīlēxī tum tē nōn tantum ut vulgus amīcam, sed pater ut gnātōs dīligit et generōs

    I loved you then not just as the crowd loves a girlfriend, but as a father loves his sons and sons-in-law.Catull. 72.3–4

    In the entry for love

  • nōn amō tē, Sabidī, nec possum dīcere quārē: hoc tantum possum dīcere, nōn amō tē

    I don’t love you, Sabidius, and I can’t say why; all I can say is this: I don’t love you.Mart. 1.32.1–2

    In the entry for love
